skill.name: discover-skills
skill.description: Finds candidate AI skills for a task by querying the SkillRadar discovery service with the task goal, constraints, and keywords.
skill.summary: Queries SkillRadar and returns a focused shortlist of skills for a specific task.
skill.author: zhiyuzi

security_audit.summary: The review confirms real network use, local script execution, hidden skill directory installation guidance, and a remote ZIP installation workflow. Many Markdown backtick and entropy findings are false positives, but the remaining issues create privacy and supply-chain risk. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote ZIP packages can be installed without integrity verification.
remediation.suggestion: Require checksums or signatures for each install_url and verify them before extracting any package.

remediation.issue: Skill recommendations can lead to persistent global installs in hidden agent directories.
remediation.suggestion: Default to project-level installation and require explicit user confirmation for any global hidden-directory install.

remediation.issue: Task goal, constraints, and keywords are sent to an external API.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users what data will be sent and ask before sending sensitive or private task context.

remediation.issue: The bash example mixes shell execution with user-derived arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Show a safer invocation pattern that passes arguments as an array or clearly requires strict shell quoting.

finding_verdicts.reason: The script imports urllib.request and uses it to make outbound HTTP requests. Network access is the intended behavior, but it still exposes task details to a third-party service.
The API endpoint is hardcoded to api.skillradar.quest. This creates a fixed external dependency and sends discovery inputs outside the local environment.
Line 86 passes args.keywords to the API payload. The word keywords contains key as text, but no certificate, private key, or secret file is accessed.
The skill instructs the agent to run the bundled discover.py script. Executing local scripts is a real external command risk, especially for community skills.
The line documents the script path in inline Markdown code. It does not itself execute a command or interpolate user input into a shell.
The following bash example runs cd and python scripts/discover.py with user-derived task values. This is a real shell execution path and can be unsafe if arguments are not passed safely.
The finding is on a closing Markdown fence and surrounding prose. No executable command appears at this line range beyond the earlier example already adjudicated.
This is a JSON example fence, not a shell command. It shows expected API output and does not execute code.

This line explains the ?v= URL parameter in inline Markdown code. It does not invoke a process or evaluate code.
The line describes choosing a project or global install directory using inline paths. It is filesystem guidance, not command execution.
The inline code lists Claude Code skill directories. No shell execution is requested on this line.

The inline code lists Codex CLI skill directories. This is path documentation, not a command invocation.
The inline code lists Gemini CLI skill directories. It does not execute or instruct a shell command.
The line instructs downloading a remote ZIP, which is a supply-chain concern captured semantically, but this static pattern is only Markdown inline code and not direct command execution.
This is a plain Markdown code fence for a ZIP directory tree example. It contains no command execution.
This is a Markdown code fence boundary and section text. It does not run a command.
The line uses inline code for field names such as name and description. It is not shell execution.
This is a JSON example fence for an empty result. It does not contain an executable command.
This is a Markdown fence boundary and service unavailable heading. It is not command execution.
This is a JSON example fence for an error response. It is documentation, not a shell or Ruby execution primitive.
The example output includes a hardcoded CDN URL for a skill ZIP package. Even as an example, it documents remote package retrieval from a third-party domain.
The installation instructions explicitly point to CDN-hosted ZIP files. This confirms a network-based installation path for remote skills.
The skill documents installing into ~/.claude/skills for global Claude Code use. Writing community skill files under hidden home directories can persist behavior across projects.
The skill documents installing into ~/.config/opencode/skills. Global hidden configuration directories are persistent and can affect future agent sessions.

The same Claude Code line includes hidden project and home skill directories. Access to these paths is legitimate for installation but security-relevant.
The OpenCode line includes hidden configuration paths. Access to these paths can alter agent behavior and should be treated as security-relevant.
The Codex line includes hidden project and global skill directories. Modifying these directories can persist marketplace content for future sessions.
The Gemini line includes hidden project and home skill directories. Hidden skill directory access is expected here but remains a real persistence risk.
SKILL.md is readable Markdown with Chinese prose and examples. I found no binary, encrypted, or obfuscated payload in the file content.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Skill Installation From Unverified ZIP
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to download install_url ZIP packages and extract them into skill directories. No checksum, signature, allowlist, or package review step is required before installation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 93-106 describe downloading a remote skill.zip, extracting it into agent skill directories, and deleting the archive. The absence of integrity verification makes this a clear supply-chain risk.

semantic_findings.title: Task Details Sent to Third-Party Discovery Service
semantic_findings.description: The script sends the task goal, constraints, and keywords to the SkillRadar API. These fields may include sensitive project or user context unless the agent asks for consent first.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The payload is built from user task fields and posted to https://api.skillradar.quest. The behavior is intentional, but the skill text does not require explicit privacy disclosure before sending data.

content.user_title: Find Relevant AI Skills for a Task
content.value_statement: Choosing the right AI skill can be slow when built-in skills do not fit. This skill queries SkillRadar and returns a focused shortlist for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Extracts a task goal, optional constraints, keywords, and desired result count from a user request.
Runs the bundled discovery script from the skill directory.
Submits discovery inputs to the SkillRadar API over HTTPS.
Returns candidate skills with names, descriptions, scores, match reasons, and install URLs.
Limits requested results to a range from 1 to 20.
Provides installation path guidance for multiple agent tools.
limitations: Requires network access to the SkillRadar service.
Sends task details and keywords to an external API.
Does not verify the safety or quality of returned skills.
Installation guidance still requires user review and permission.

use_cases.title: Locate a Missing Workflow Skill
use_cases.description: Find a small set of candidate skills when existing local skills do not cover the requested task.

use_cases.title: Compare Marketplace Candidates
use_cases.description: Review candidate names, descriptions, scores, and match reasons before choosing a skill to inspect.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Controlled Installation
use_cases.description: Use the returned install URL and path guidance to plan a project-level skill installation.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Find skills that can help me summarize long meeting notes into action items. Use simple keywords and return the best candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Search With Constraints
prompt_templates.scenario: Task search with privacy or format limits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find candidate skills for extracting tables from PDFs. The skill must support CSV output and should work with local files.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Candidate Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for skills that audit Terraform files. Compare the top five results and explain which candidates look most relevant.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Install
prompt_templates.prompt: Find skills for image cleanup, then recommend only project-level installation steps. Highlight any network or package trust risks before installing.

output_examples.input: Find a skill that can merge several PDF files and handle batch processing.
output: The result is a ranked shortlist of PDF-related skills.
Each candidate includes a short description, match reasons, and an installation link.
The response notes that the user should review the package before installation.

output_examples.input: Find skills for turning research notes into a structured report.
output: The result lists writing and documentation skills that match report generation.
The strongest candidates are explained with concise match reasons.
The response asks for more detail if the task goal is too broad.

output_examples.input: Find a local-only data cleanup skill for CSV files.
output: The response searches with local-only and CSV constraints.
It warns when returned candidates do not clearly meet the local-only requirement.

best_practices: Use concise task goals, specific constraints, and three to ten relevant keywords.
Review candidate descriptions and match reasons before choosing a skill.
Prefer project-level installation unless the user explicitly approves a global install.
anti_patterns: Do not send private project details to discovery services without user consent.
Do not install a returned ZIP package without reviewing its source and contents.
Do not force a weak candidate when the results do not match the task.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It searches SkillRadar for skills that match a task goal, constraints, and keywords.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled script sends a request to the SkillRadar API.

faq.question: Can it install skills automatically?
faq.answer: The instructions include installation guidance, but users should approve and review any package first.

faq.question: What information is sent to the API?
faq.answer: The script sends the task goal, task constraints, keywords, and maximum result count.

faq.question: Does it verify returned skill packages?
faq.answer: No. The current files do not include checksum, signature, or trust verification logic.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
